fixture.candidate_text: Nora saw red clay on the storage-room floor and looked at Eli's mud-caked boots. Only the two of them knew the combination. ‘You went in there,’ she said, then added, ‘Or you want me to think you didn't.’
authoritative_context: Nora did not directly see Eli enter the room.
Eli had just returned from the red-clay construction site.
Only Nora and Eli know the combination.

rule_check.statement: A character must not use knowledge unavailable to them without a plausible narrative basis.

rubric: First decide whether the knowledge-boundary rule is applicable; then decide whether the character's claim is direct knowledge, plausible inference, or unsupported omniscience.
A plausible inference from visible evidence must not be failed merely because the inferred event was not directly observed.
Accept when the candidate has a sufficient narrative basis and preserves uncertainty.
